title: Mid-Century Modern — One bright idea, a connected system

scenes.title: Poster fields and figure
scenes.purpose: Set up a dusk-slate mid-century poster: an organic mustard field, a geometric teal quarter-field, the headline, and a simple figure rising into frame.
visuals: Mustard kidney field scales and turns in
Teal quarter-circle grows from the lower-right corner
Teal body rises, ink head settles, arm dips then starts its swing
Seeded cream and ink print grain, stationary

beats.development: The colour fields establish the composition. Headline 'One bright idea,' and subhead 'A CONNECTED SYSTEM' slide in.
The figure rises onto the mustard field. The head settles and the arm dips down in anticipation.

scenes.title: The idea ignites
scenes.purpose: The raised hand produces the idea: a cream halo, a brick-red star and a Canvas 2D atomic starburst.
visuals: Canvas mustard and cream rays grow and turn

beats.development: The star appears at the hand and the starburst rays extend.

scenes.title: Idea becomes a system
scenes.purpose: Cream links draw out from the star, and nodes pop in as each line arrives. The poster then settles and holds so the copy can be read.
visuals: Five cream links draw in sequence via stroke-dashoffset
Brick, teal and mustard nodes with cream rims pop in on arrival

beats.development: The network grows from the idea into four connected nodes. The accents and the tagline 'DESIGNED FOR LIVING TOGETHER' settle.
Settled poster hold. All copy is legible.

findings: The colour fields and headline arrive in the first 0.6s, so the viewer gets the context first.
The arm gets anticipation (a dip) before its swing, and the star ignites on the swing's follow-through.
Links draw one after another so the eye follows the network from the star to the farthest node.
Everything is settled by about 2.45s, before the 2.7s requirement.
justifiedHolds: 2.45–3.0s hold so the full composition and all three lines of copy can be read.

notes: No reviewed preview recipes were supplied (empty list). This preview shows the base style implementation: geometric and organic paths, layered figure and props, and seeded grain.
BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json lists 0 matched sources and no contact sheets. The scene-dependent dusk-slate background comes from the brief's subject and mood, not from source evidence.
Blender is not used, per the user instruction.
Layering: colour fields (SVG), then Canvas starburst, then figure and system (SVG), then seeded grain (Canvas), then copy (SVG). The copy sits above the grain so no text is occluded.
